what_its_for: Ketoconazole cream is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal and yeast infections of the skin. It works by killing the fungus or yeast that is causing your infection. Common conditions it treats include ringworm (tinea corporis), athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), tinea versicolor (a skin discoloration caused by yeast), and seborrheic dermatitis (a scaly, itchy skin rash). It helps relieve itching, redness, flaking, and burning caused by these infections.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only. Do not swallow it, put it in your eyes, or use it inside your nose, mouth, or vagina. Before applying, wash and dry the affected area thoroughly. Squeeze a small amount of cream onto your fingertip and apply a thin layer to cover the infected area and about one inch of the surrounding skin. Gently rub it in. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or tight wrappings unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Apply the cream once daily to the affected area. Your doctor may sometimes recommend twice daily application depending on your condition. The length of treatment depends on what you are treating: ringworm and jock itch usually require 2 to 4 weeks of treatment, athlete's foot usually requires 4 to 6 weeks, tinea versicolor usually requires 2 weeks, and seborrheic dermatitis may require 4 to 6 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and complete the full course of treatment even if your symptoms improve early.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed dose. Try to apply the cream at the same time each day to help you remember.
storage: Store the cream at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and open flame. Do not freeze the cream. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream after the expiration date printed on the tube or box. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused or expired cream.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the cream in your eyes, mouth, nose, or other mucous membranes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Avoid wearing tight or non-breathable clothing over treated areas, as this can make the infection worse. For athlete's foot, avoid walking barefoot in public places and change your socks daily. For jock itch, wear loose-fitting clothing. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or personal items with others while you have an active infection. Do not use other skin products, lotions, or cosmetics on the treated area unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical attention if you experience any of the following: signs of an allergic reaction such as severe rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; increased redness, burning, swelling, or irritation at the application site that gets worse instead of better; blistering, oozing, or open sores develop on the treated skin; your infection does not improve after 2 weeks of treatment or gets worse at any time; you develop a fever or feel very unwell; or you develop unusual skin discoloration or peeling beyond what was originally there.
when_it_works: Most people start to notice some improvement in their symptoms such as reduced itching, redness, and scaling within the first 2 to 4 weeks of using ketoconazole cream. However, it is very important to continue using the cream for the full length of time your doctor prescribed, even if you feel better sooner. Stopping treatment too early can allow the infection to come back. If you do not see any improvement after 2 weeks of consistent use, call your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this cream. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. If breastfeeding, avoid applying the cream to the breast or nipple area to prevent the baby from accidentally swallowing it. Children: This cream can generally be used in children, but always follow your doctor's guidance for the correct amount and length of treatment in children. Elderly patients: No special dosing adjustments are needed for older adults, but if your skin is very thin or sensitive, let your doctor know. People with skin conditions: Tell your doctor if you have any other skin conditions such as eczema or psoriasis, as these may affect how your skin responds to this cream.
